name: S. Daniel Abraham
profile: Founder of Slim-Fast (sold to Unilever for $2.3B in 2000) and founder of the S. Daniel Abraham Center for Middle East Peace. Died June 29, 2025 in New York City at age 100.
notes: Deceased (June 29, 2025, per JTA obituary and Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._Daniel_Abraham). Skip.

name: Susan Hirt Hagen
profile: Daughter of Erie Insurance co-founder H.O. Hirt and longest-serving Erie Indemnity board member (first woman on the board, 1980). Died June 15, 2015 at age 79.
notes: Deceased (June 15, 2015, per Erie Insurance press release). Skip.

name: Stefan Schoerghuber
profile: Owner and CEO of Munich's Schörghuber Unternehmensgruppe (construction/real estate, brewing via Paulaner/BrauHolding, hotels), which he took over after his father Josef died in 1995. Died unexpectedly 25 November 2008 aged 47; widow Alexandra Schörghuber later led the group.
notes: Deceased (25 Nov 2008, per Wikipedia and Brauwelt https://brauwelt.com/en/international-report/europe-russia/626074-brewer-and-hotelier-stefan-schrghuber-dies-at-47). Skip.

name: Ronald Owen Perelman
current_role: Chairman & CEO, MacAndrews & Forbes Incorporated (New York); Chairman of Carnegie Hall since 2015
profile: Wharton-trained financier who built MacAndrews & Forbes, his wholly owned holding company, through leveraged buyouts from 1978 on, most famously Revlon; holdings have included Deluxe/Vericast, SIGA Technologies and Scientific Games. Since 2020 he has sold assets and the firm reportedly now operates more like a family office.
interesting_fact: He has been chairman of Carnegie Hall since May 2015 and gave $75 million toward the performing arts center at the World Trade Center site, which bears his name.
deep_cut_fact: His first big deal came in 1961 as a Wharton freshman: with his father he bought Philadelphia's Esslinger Brewery for $800,000 and sold it three years later for a $1 million profit. By age 11 he was regularly sitting in on his father's Belmont Iron Works board meetings.
notes: Net worth fell sharply since 2018 peak; avoid wealth/litigation topics. Best route is MacAndrews & Forbes contact form. Carnegie Hall connection is a warm, positive angle.

name: S Gopalakrishnan
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund/accelerator); co-founder of Infosys; Chair, IISc Council
profile: Senapathy 'Kris' Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and was its CEO/MD (2007-2011) and vice chairman (2011-2014). He now backs startups through Axilor Ventures and family investment arm Pratithi, and funds neuroscience and research through the Pratiksha Trust, while chairing IISc's Council and several Indian government innovation bodies.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 2.25 billion to build the Centre for Brain Research at IISc, described as the largest individual gift the institute has received, and funds a cellular-level brain-mapping centre at IIT Madras.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a physicist, earning an M.Sc. in Physics (1977) before an M.Tech in Computer Science (1979) at IIT Madras, and his first job was as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in Mumbai in 1979, where he met the future Infosys founding team.
notes: Goes by 'Kris'. Very active public speaker on AI, deep tech and startups (CII, IISc); good podcast fit. Axilor's general inbox is the best published route; the Pratiksha Trust site lists no email.

name: Sid Richardson Bass
current_role: Private investor and philanthropist, Fort Worth, Texas (head of the Bass family investment group since 1968)
profile: Fort Worth oil heir (grand-nephew of wildcatter Sid W. Richardson) who took control of the family business in 1968 and, per Vanity Fair, grew a ~$50M company into a ~$14B investment group. With his brothers he was Disney's largest shareholder from 1984 and is known for backing Michael Eisner's management. Yale 1965, Stanford MBA.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he and then-wife Mercedes Bass gave $25 million to the Metropolitan Opera, at the time the largest individual gift in the company's history.
deep_cut_fact: At just 28 he and his then-wife commissioned Paul Rudolph to design the Bass Residence in Fort Worth's Westover Hills, often called Rudolph's most ambitious residential project; it received the AIA Fort Worth chapter's 25 Year Honor Award in 2005.
notes: Very private; no published personal office email, website or social accounts found. Family office (Bass Enterprises, Fort Worth) does not publish contacts. Best route is likely a warm intro via Fort Worth civic/arts circles.

name: Dennis Bastas
current_role: Chairman and Group CEO, DBG Health (Melbourne)
profile: Melbourne-born son of Greek migrants who started in logistics at Coles Myer, founded generics maker Genepharm Australasia in the early 2000s and sold it to Watson in 2012 for $252M. His DBG Health bought Arrotex Pharmaceuticals and others in 2023, and in 2025 BDT & MSD Partners bought a stake in DBG's holding company for $1B, valuing it at over $4.7B.
interesting_fact: DBG Health's 2023 deals, worth $671M, included Arrotex Pharmaceuticals, Australia's largest pharmaceutical company by market share.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an industrial designer, graduating in Engineering & Industrial Design from Monash University in 1988 and hoping to design cars overseas. The early-1990s recession changed his plans and he took a logistics job at Coles Myer instead.
notes: DBG's contact form explicitly accepts media/press enquiries; state the purpose in the form. Car design and industrial design are a natural conversation opener. Coles Myer detail also in the ReadyMedia profile https://content.readymedia.com.au/video/dennis-bastas

name: Ron Burkle
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, The Yucaipa Companies (Los Angeles); co-owner, Pittsburgh Penguins
profile: Pomona-born son of a Stater Bros. store manager who founded Yucaipa in 1986 and made his fortune buying and merging supermarket chains (Fred Meyer, Ralphs, Food4Less, Dominick's). He now invests mainly in food-trade logistics, cold storage and food safety, and in 2026 led a group that took Soho House private.
interesting_fact: He bought Jesse Owens' 1936 Berlin Olympic gold medal at auction for about $1.4-1.5 million in 2013, and with Mario Lemieux he brought the Pittsburgh Penguins out of bankruptcy in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: By age 13 he had joined the grocery workers' union, UFCW Local 770, while stocking shelves at his father's store. He finished high school at 16 and went to Cal Poly Pomona to study dentistry before leaving for the grocery business.
notes: Yucaipa press relations email is the best published route. Also co-chairs UCLA's Burkle Center for International Relations. Avoid Epstein/Clinton-related topics.

name: Hiroshi Mikitani
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Rakuten Group, Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Kobe-born ex-Industrial Bank of Japan banker (Harvard MBA 1993) who founded Rakuten in 1997 and built it into one of Japan's biggest e-commerce, fintech and telecom groups, including the 2020 launch of Rakuten Mobile. Through Rakuten he is also a 10%+ owner of satellite-to-phone company AST SpaceMobile.
interesting_fact: In 2010 he made English Rakuten's official internal language ('Englishnization'), later a Harvard Business Review case study. In 2011 he quit Keidanren after Fukushima, partly over its backing for continued reliance on nuclear power.
deep_cut_fact: Rakuten Ichiba went live on May 1, 1997 with just 13 shops and 6 employees, funded with $250,000 of the founders' own money. As a boy he lived in New Haven, Connecticut (1972-74) while his economist father taught at Yale.
notes: Nickname 'Mickey'. Strong podcast angles: Rakuten Mobile, AST SpaceMobile, his public position on energy policy after Fukushima. Avoid Rakuten's losses. Media enquiries go through the Rakuten press contact form.

name: Kim Beom-su
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of Kakao Corp. (Seoul); left the chairmanship and board in 2022 (any 2026 executive role not confirmed)
profile: Also known as Brian Kim. He grew up poor in Seoul, studied engineering at Seoul National University, founded online gaming portal Hangame (merged with Naver to form NHN) and launched KakaoTalk in 2010, now on about 90% of Korean smartphones. Kakao expanded into payments, mobility, games and banking, and he backs startups through K Cube Ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he became one of the first Korean signers of the Giving Pledge, committing more than half his wealth to charity. He paid his way through college as a private tutor, sometimes skipping meals to save money.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a developer for an online communication service at Samsung's IT services unit. Hangame, founded in 1998 with $184,000 from friends and family, started as an internet café business before becoming Korea's first online gaming portal. In 2006 he set up IWILAB, a Mountain View incubator for Korean founders.
notes: Avoid the 2024 SM Entertainment stock case (acquitted Oct 2025) and gambling allegations. No published personal channel found. Kakao's press room is the corporate media route; its media contact details load dynamically and were not captured. Web search budget ran out before his 2026 role could be checked.

name: Douglas Hsu Hsu-Tung
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Far Eastern Group (Taipei); re-elected chairman of Asia Cement in 2026
profile: Douglas Tong Hsu (徐旭東) is the son of founder Yu-Ziang Hsu and heads Far Eastern Group, a Taiwanese conglomerate of about 250 companies and nine listed firms. Its businesses span petrochemicals and energy (including Chiahui Power), polyester, cement, telecom (Far EasTone), banking, retail (SOGO, Far Eastern Department Stores) and hotels. Son Jeff Hsu debuted as group Chief Innovation Officer at 2026 AGMs.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Far Eastern New Century became the world's third-largest polyester textile maker (2018), and the group's family foundations established leading private universities and a medical-centre hospital in Taiwan.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BA and MA at the University of Notre Dame, where he is an Emeritus Trustee, followed by postgraduate study at Columbia. His Committee of 100 profile calls him an 'architecture devotee' and collector of modern art and sculpture who enjoys diving and swimming.
notes: No personal or press email published on the FEG site (the only email listed is a mall customer-service address, so it is excluded). Energy and telecom holdings make him a podcast fit; best route is via group corporate communications or Far EasTone/FENC investor relations. Member of the Committee of 100 since 2005.

name: Lottie Tham
current_role: Private investor; major H&M shareholder (no operating role at H&M)
profile: Helga Liselott 'Lottie' Tham (née Persson, b. 1949) is the daughter of H&M founder Erling Persson and the sister of former chairman Stefan Persson, and holds over 5% of H&M. With her husband, financier Pieter Tham, she invests in real estate including hotels, commercial buildings and land. She deliberately keeps out of the public eye.
interesting_fact: Her father got the idea for H&M (founded 1947 as Hennes in Västerås) on a road trip through the US after seeing New York's department stores.
notes: Very private, with no public role, website, social media or published office contact. Little energy/tech relevance. Low-priority outreach target; any approach would need a warm introduction.

name: Xu Cheng
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/CEO of Hsu Fu Chi (徐福记); retired from the business after Nestlé bought the family's remaining stake in 2025
profile: Taiwan-born Hsu Chen (徐乘, b. 1952), the second-oldest of four brothers, co-founded confectioner Hsu Fu Chi, which set up in Dongguan in 1992 and became China's second-largest candy company after Mars. Nestlé bought 60% in 2011 for about $1.7B with Hsu staying on as chairman/CEO, and acquired the family's remaining 40% in 2025.
interesting_fact: Hsu Fu Chi became China's best-known Chinese New Year candy brand and grew into the country's No. 2 confectioner, which led to Nestlé's roughly $1.7B purchase of a controlling stake in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: The Hsu Fu Chi brand began in Taiwan in 1976, started by Hsu Chen and his brothers, 16 years before they moved the business to Dongguan in 1992 and built it into a mainland giant.
notes: Low profile and has left the business, with no personal office, website or social media found. Deep-cut source is a user-contributed Chinese profile site (moderate confidence); English sources give 1992 as the Dongguan founding date. Low relevance to energy/data-center themes.

name: Jack Cowin
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Competitive Foods Australia (Hungry Jack's); Chairman and largest shareholder, Domino's Pizza Enterprises
profile: Born in Windsor, Ontario, he moved to Perth in 1969 to open KFC franchises, then founded Hungry Jack's as Australia's Burger King franchisee. He also chairs and is the top shareholder of ASX-listed Domino's Pizza Enterprises, and owns plant-based meat maker v2food, meat processor Consolidated Foods and 40% of BridgeClimb Sydney.
interesting_fact: He is rolling out EV fast-charging units at his drive-through restaurants. He took the name Hungry Jack's only because someone else already held the Burger King trademark in Australia.
deep_cut_fact: He financed his first KFC outlets in Perth in December 1969 by raising C$10,000 each from thirty Canadians, after four years selling insurance for London Life in Toronto. As a student at Western Ontario he sold trees, shrubs and rocks, and later served as the university's chancellor (2015-2019).
notes: Good fit for an energy episode: EV charging at drive-throughs, plus v2food. Domino's IR email is the most direct published corporate address. Hungry Jack's lists only a customer-service email, so use its contact page for a media request.

name: Luo Hongxia
current_role: Listed by Hurun alongside Wang Chenghai as holder of Dongguan Dingtong Precision Technology (鼎通科技, SSE STAR 688668) wealth; personal role not confirmed
profile: Hurun attributes her wealth, shared with Wang Chenghai, to Dongguan Dingtong Precision Technology. Dingtong was founded in 2003 as a precision hardware maker and listed on the STAR Market, and makes precision components for high-speed communication connectors and automotive connectors. Chairman Wang Chenghai (b. 1970) has led the company since 2003.
interesting_fact: Dingtong's core products are precision parts for high-speed communication connectors, the kind of interconnect used in telecom and data-center hardware, which ties this fortune to the AI/data-center build-out.
notes: No public source found naming Luo Hongxia's role at Dingtong or her relation to Wang Chenghai, so identity is left uncertain. Chairman Wang Chenghai (Tsinghua EMBA 2024) is the public face; company background: https://finance.ifeng.com/c/8wWTzMFkgXZ . Approach via Dingtong's investor-relations channel listed in its SSE filings.

name: Herbert Allen Jr
current_role: Former president (now senior figure and controlling family member) of Allen & Company, New York; son Herbert Allen III has run the firm since 2002
profile: Joined his uncle Charles's boutique investment bank Allen & Co. straight out of Williams College in 1962 and became president in 1966 at 26. The firm bought control of Columbia Pictures in 1973 and sold it to Coca-Cola in 1982, giving him a long-time Coke board seat. It advised on major tech deals and IPOs and hosts the invitation-only Sun Valley conference.
interesting_fact: He launched the Allen & Co. Sun Valley Conference in 1982, the 'summer camp for billionaires' where media and tech leaders such as Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg have gathered. He is also the largest individual holder of Coca-Cola stock.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Irvington, New York, joined Allen & Co. the year he left Williams College (1962), and became its president at 26. In 1998 he gave $20 million back to Williams.
notes: Allen & Co. is famously discreet: no public website, press office or published email. Now based in Cody, Wyoming (per Wikipedia), aged about 86. Realistic route is a warm introduction via the Sun Valley network or Herbert Allen III.

name: Inder Jaisinghani
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Polycab India Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Mumbai entrepreneur who, with his brothers, grew the family's small electrical-goods shop in Lohar Chawl into Polycab India, the country's largest wires-and-cables maker. Polycab added fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear from 2014, listed in 2019, and runs 28 plants exporting to 79 countries. The World Bank's IFC took a stake in 2008.
interesting_fact: Polycab grew from a trading firm started in 1986 into a listed manufacturer with 28 plants across India selling to 79 countries, supplying the cables behind India's power, infrastructure and data-centre build-out.
deep_cut_fact: Before Polycab became an industrial giant, the Jaisinghani brothers began their first wire-manufacturing experiments in a garage of about 100 square feet in Mumbai, while still running the family's electrical shop in Lohar Chawl.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (power cables, grid and data-centre electrification). Low media profile. Polycab IR is the best published route. Deep-cut detail comes from YourStory (blocked to direct fetch) and was corroborated in search snippets from several Indian outlets, including DNA India.

name: Liu Fangyi
current_role: Founder & Chairman, INTCO Medical Technology (Shenzhen-listed, Zibo, Shandong); also founder & chairman of INTCO Recycling
profile: Liu Fangyi, known internationally as Frank Liu, founded INTCO Medical's predecessor in Zibo in 2009 and listed it in Shenzhen in 2017. It became one of the world's largest disposable-glove makers and expanded into rehabilitation equipment, monitoring and personal care, with 2025 revenue of RMB 9.93B. He also chairs listed plastics recycler INTCO Recycling.
interesting_fact: He chairs two separately listed companies, a glove/medical-consumables maker and a plastics-recycling firm. In July 2026 he was named a New Fortune 'Best Industry Excellence Leader of the Year', and INTCO Recycling won an ESG Best Practice award.
deep_cut_fact: Before medical gloves, his first venture was recycling: he founded INTCO Recycling (英科再生) in 2005 to recycle plastics, four years before starting the medical business. In 2017 he was named to China's national 'Ten Thousand Talents' programme as a tech-entrepreneurship leader.
notes: Uses the English name 'Frank Liu'. The recycling/circular-economy angle (INTCO Recycling) may suit an energy/industry podcast better than gloves. The 2005 founding date for INTCO Recycling comes from Chinese business-media search results (36Kr, rmlt.com.cn).
